sovereign_country.strategic_role: 连接拉美市场的欧洲商贸桥梁、本地化仓配与数字游民签证

business_scope.primary_industry_name: AAA Game Asset 3D Sculpting and Character Rigging Studio

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (national unitary jurisdiction; no sub-state company registry)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental European notarial system; corporate law codified in Ley de Sociedades de Capital 1/2010)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Double Taxation Conventions with Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Peru, Uruguay and other Latin American states

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, implementing the AML regulatory framework; Real Decreto 1517/2018, de 19 de octubre, creating and regulating the Spanish central Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO / titular real) register; Ley 12/2003, de 21 de mayo, de prevención y bloqueo de la financiación del terrorismo.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each UBO and director, with certified Spanish translation if issued in a non-Spanish language
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport/police office of each UBO's country of origin, plus certified translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or corporate registry extract for any UBO that is a legal entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the UBO's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or Consular Legalization if the issuer is not a Hague Convention member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney granting authority to the Spanish incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's country of residence, translated into Spanish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record certificate of each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Justice / national police records authority in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO for AML verification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Fully regulated bank or public utility provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization locally; no consular legalization required if apostille-eligible

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against: (a) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list; (b) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (c) EU consolidated financial sanctions list; and (d) Spanish SEPBLAC and Ministry of Finance warning lists. PEP status must be verified through a licensed financial intelligence provider; positive PEP hits trigger enhanced customer due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, and senior management approval. ISIC 7490 is classified as 'Low_Risk_Standard' for AML purposes, but Article 3 of Ley 10/2010 still mandates full identification of the UBO and sanctions screening before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central, RMC) - online negative name certificate application through the official registradores portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must use the Latin alphabet and may be in Spanish or any official language of Spain or the European Union. Non-Latin-script names and UBO names must be transliterated into Latin script. The name must not be identical or phonetically equivalent to any existing Spanish registered company and must include 'S.L.' or 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Sector-regulated words such as 'Energía', 'Telecomunicaciones', 'Juego', 'Sanidad', 'Inversión', 'Valores' without a licence or regulatory authorization
Words implying public authority, institutional status, or misleading geographical provenance
Identical or phonetically similar tokens of pre-existing Spanish companies in any industry
Blasphemous, indecent, misleading, or contrary to law expressions
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If RMC rejects a name application: (1) obtain the written refusal; (2) correct transcription or prohibited-token defects and refile; (3) file an administrative appeal ('recurso de alzada') with the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within one month of refusal; (4) if the rejection is upheld, request a fresh negative certificate using two alternative names in priority order.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is acceptable only if it provides a genuine physical correspondence address in Spain and the SL maintains substantive commercial presence, such as payroll, equipment, or management in Spain. For an ISIC 7490 game-art BPO, pure mail-forwarding virtual offices may be challenged as sham under tax-residence and commercial-substance rules; a co-working or telework hub with documented operations is preferred.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 10-15% annual likelihood of an unannounced commercial-registry or law-enforcement substance inspection for a low-risk creative BPO; risk exceeds 40% if the SL has no employees, no lease, or frequent UBO changes.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Negative name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación social) at Registro Mercantil Central
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RMC fee, approximately EUR 14-40 depending on online filing mode

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial execution of deed of incorporation and bylaws (escritura de constitución and estatutos sociales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish notary assigned under the Notarial College
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff under Real Decreto 1426/1989, value-linked and folio-count basis

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Registry deposit and inscription of the newly formed SL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing tariff of the Registro Mercantil, based on official fee tables

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration filing in the Spanish central titular-real register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial / Spanish central UBO register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for filing via registered agent; no direct statutory fee in most provinces

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization / Hague Apostille of passport, good-standing, criminal-record, and power-of-attorney documents (bundle of four)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Consulates and Ministries of Foreign Affairs of UBO countries / Spanish consular posts
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document consular or apostille fee, typically USD 30-90 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting and AML/UBO due-diligence advisory package for SL incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a small SL with non-resident UBOs, 3-5 lawyer hours

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Application for provisional CIF/NIF and social security employer code (código de cuenta de cotización)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee; zero-cost direct electronic filing

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Texto Refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC), arts. 3-4, 11, 20-22, 121-124, 175-180; Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece), arts. 2-3 on digital incorporation and reduced minimum capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central for the negative name certificate; Registro Mercantil y de Bienes Muebles de Madrid for company registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial public deed of incorporation (Escritura de Constitución) filed with the Mercantile Registry together with the application for registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SL has no statutory minimum above €1; if share capital is set below €3,000, at least 20% of annual profits must be allocated to a legal reserve until capital plus legal reserve equals €3,000. All cash contributions must be fully paid and deposited at the time the deed is granted; no escrow or notarial escrow account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At a duly convened general meeting of the sole incorporator/shareholder held in Madrid on [date], it was resolved: (1) To subscribe and fully pay the share capital of €1,000 divided into 1,000 indivisible quotas, as set out in the deed; (2) To adopt the Articles of Association, approve the corporate purpose covering 3D art and character rigging services, and adopt the registered office at Calle Gran Vía 28, Madrid; (3) To appoint the sole administrator and shareholder as legal representative with powers for banking, contracting, and licensing; (4) To authorize filing with the Mercantile Registry, obtaining the Tax Identification Number, and commencing operations upon inscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Negative denomination certificate from the Central Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central via its online application platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an electronic request for a certificación negativa de denominación choosing up to five proposed SL names. The Central Registry verifies that no identical or confusingly similar company name exists in Spain. The certificate is usually issued within three business days and is valid for three months; attach it to the incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Request form with proposed corporate names
Power of attorney if filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a proposed name is refused, file a new request with fresh alternatives or submit a written reconsideration. The Registry will issue a new certificate if the alternative names are available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a provisional bank account and deposit of paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved Spanish credit institution selected by the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the company under formation and deposit the fully paid cash contribution of €1,000. Obtain a bank certificate evidencing the deposit, which must be submitted to the notary. The account is converted into the company's operating account after registration.
required_dossiers: Provisional NIF of the company under formation, if obtainable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the corporate details, correct the discrepancies and obtain a revised deposit certificate. If the bank refuses the profile, select another authorized credit institution and repeat the process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Granting of the public deed of incorporation before a notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the Madrid Notarial College
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary with the founders, the negative name certificate, bank deposit certificate, proposed Articles of Association, and identity documents. The notary reviews legal capacity, verifies the corporate purpose, and executes the public deed with signatures. Under Law 18/2022, the deed may be executed and signed digitally using qualified electronic certificates.
required_dossiers: Bank deposit certificate or proof of fully paid capital
DNI, NIE, or passport of each incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects, remedy them by amending the deed clauses or submitting additional documentation. If the notary refuses execution, choose another notary and resubmit the corrected file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF provisional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form 036 to AEAT declaring the company as 'sociedad en constitución' before or immediately after execution of the deed. AEAT assigns the provisional NIF, which must be stated in the public deed and used on all pre-registration documents.
required_dossiers: Signed copy of the notarial deed or deed draft
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT issues a subsanación request, correct the form or legal wording and resubmit within the stated deadline. Failure to cure may require a supplementary notarial deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Formal registration of the incorporated company in the Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil y de Bienes Muebles de Madrid
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the first notarial copy of the deed, the name certificate, Form 036 proof, and payment evidence of any applicable transfer-tax document to the Provincial Mercantile Registry. The Registrar verifies all clauses and, upon approval, issues the registration certificate. Full legal personality is acquired only after inscription.
required_dossiers: First notarial copy of the public deed
Proof of payment of corporate capital tax or exemption, if liable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry files a nota de defectos, correct the formal defects by a supplemental deed or by completing missing documents, then resubmit. If its position is legally wrong, appeal the registrar's decision to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within two months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Danish Tax Agency; here AEAT local office corresponding to the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Mercantile Registry inscription, present the registration certificate and the notarial deed to AEAT. AEAT converts the provisional NIF into the definitive NIF and issues the updated tax identification card. This NIF must be used on all invoices and tax filings.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT does not convert the NIF due to address or legal-form mismatches, correct Form 036 and present a certified copy of the final registration. Administrative errors are cured by reopening the file in the competent AEAT unit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer registration with Social Security and occupational risk prevention (PRL) onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS) and an accredited external prevention service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SL as an employer by obtaining a código de cuenta de cotización, declare the 3D art studio activity, and arrange a workplace risk assessment covering screen-intensive work, electrical equipment, and server-room hazards. Before hiring employees, obtain the PRL service contract and initial assessment report.
required_dossiers: PRL risk assessment report from accredited service
Lease or ownership title of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If TGSS rejects the employer code, correct the reported activity codes or address. If the PRL report identifies deficiencies, implement corrective measures and obtain a revised assessment before commencing operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal declaration of responsible activity and fire-safety/civil defense clearance for office studio
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ayuntamiento de Madrid – Urban Planning and Economic Activities Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the declaración responsable de inicio de actividad for an office/creative studio at the registered premises. Provide technical certificates confirming that the floor area, emergency exits, and fire-fighting equipment comply with the local fire code. The municipality may inspect the premises within 30 days and issue an occupancy clearance if no defects are found.
required_dossiers: Fire installation and electrical safety certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the post-declaration inspection finds deviations, remedy the defects within 15 days and request a re-inspection. If the activity exceeds declared surface area or risk limits, file a full municipal activity license under the applicable urban ordinance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Consejería de Economía, Hacienda y Empleo – Dirección General de Industria, Energía y Minas de la Comunidad de Madrid
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No mandatory operating or manufacturing license; the office-based 3D art outsourcing activity is subject only to the municipal declaration of responsible activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Dirección General de Sostenibilidad y Economía Circular – Consejería de Medio Ambiente, Agricultura e Interior de la Comunidad de Madrid
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Annex II low-risk office and creative studio activity; no full EIA report or environmental registration required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater generated; sanitary and stormwater discharges must comply with Madrid municipal sewer ordinances (BOD5 < 300 mg/l, TSS < 300 mg/l, pH 6-9). Volatile organic compound emissions from printing or resin modeling must remain below 20 mg/Nm3 or use best available techniques; hazardous waste such as inks, solvents, and electronic scrap shall be stored separately and consigned to an authorized manager.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification for office/studio occupancy with fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, and evacuation signage; building structural load inspection confirming safe office use; workplace health and safety clearance under Law 31/1995 and Royal Decree 486/1997, including ergonomic workstations, ventilation, and electrical installation checks.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); official electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es); corporate income tax returns via Modelo 200/220; VAT via Modelos 303/349/390; customs delegated to Dependencia de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation of the SL before a Spanish notary, the promoter obtains a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) by filing Modelo 036 at the competent provincial AEAT office. After inscription in the Registro Mercantil, the provisional NIF becomes definitive; the entity then files Modelo 036 to obtain the definitive NIF certificate. Simultaneously, the SL registers for VAT (IVA) on the same Modelo 036, thereby obtaining the NIF-IVA (format ES-B[8 digits][control]). Foreign shareholders or group entities without a Spanish permanent establishment must obtain a non-resident NIF with prefix 'N' via Modelo 036 and, if not established in the EU/EEA, appoint a resident tax representative (representante fiscal) when required by law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Spanish-resident SL is an opaque taxpayer subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (CIT) under Ley 27/2014 (TRLIS) at a standard 25% rate; new entities enjoy a reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 300,000 of taxable base for their first two profitable years; the SL is never fiscally transparent in Spain.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists; the SL is mandatorily opaque. Available elections include: (i) CIT group consolidation (Arts. 64-111 TRLIS) where a Spanish parent holds at least 75% (70% for listed entities) of a subsidiary; (ii) reduced CIT rate for newly incorporated entities (Art. 29.2 TRLIS); (iii) patent box regime (Art. 23 TRLIS) for qualifying IP income; (iv) VAT refund fast-track via REDEME monthly regime; (v) cash-basis VAT for SMEs with turnover below EUR 2,000,000; (vi) intra-community VAT grouping under Arts. 163 bis decies et seq. Ley IVA; and (vii) election to claim EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive zero withholding on dividends. ATAD II hybrid rules (Art. 15ter TRLIS) may re-characterise the SL as a reverse hybrid if all non-resident direct or indirect shareholders are located in jurisdictions that treat the SL as transparent.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT / IVA (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido) regulated by Ley 37/1992 and RD 1624/1992, aligned with EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC; reverse charge mechanism applies to cross-border B2B supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 — no de minimis turnover threshold; every taxable person carrying out taxable supplies in Spain must register via Modelo 036 before commencing operations. For intra-community acquisitions by non-deductible persons, the annual exemption threshold is EUR 10,000; a fully taxable SL is outside this exception and must at all times hold a valid NIF-IVA for intra-EU trade.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) is mandatory for taxpayers with turnover exceeding EUR 6,010,121.04, VAT groups and REDEME registrants; invoice records must be transmitted to AEAT through SII web services (SOAP/XML with X.509 certificate, Facturae 3.2 format) within 4 business days (8 calendar days for bulk simplified submissions). For all other SLs, Ley 18/2022 Crea y Crece mandates B2B electronic invoicing once the implementing royal decree is in force (expected during 2025). Verifactu (RD 1007/2023) requires qualified billing software generating hash-chained invoice records identified by 'VERI*FACTU' from 1 July 2025; no real-time fiscal stamp is required pre-clearance, but invoice records must be accessible to AEAT during inspection and may include a QR verification code.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: An SL may apply 0% VAT (exemption with right to deduction) to: (i) exports of goods physically leaving the EU customs territory (Art. 21 Ley IVA), provided exit is evidenced within 90 days; (ii) intra-EU B2B supplies of services under Art. 69(1) Ley IVA where the customer is established in another Member State and holds a valid VAT number, with the invoice citing 'inversión del sujeto pasivo'; and (iii) services to customers established outside the EU (Art. 69 Ley IVA), including digital game art, 3D sculpting, rigging and asset licensing, where such services are not effectively connected to Spanish immovable property or on-site work in Spain. Substantiation requires an enforceable service contract, complete digital delivery logs, valid foreign tax identification of the customer, and proof of payment; the corresponding input VAT remains fully deductible subject to the pro-rata rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Documento Único Administrativo) with the assigned EORI reference and customs exit stamp or NCTS/EXS electronic exit confirmation
Transport document evidencing physical exit from the EU: Bill of Lading, Air Waybill (AWB), CMR consignment note or rail/sea manifest
Commercial invoice with HS classification of exported media (e.g., HS 8523 for digital game assets embodied on physical media) and Incoterms 2020
Packing list and value declaration supporting the declared export amount
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de divisas) or SWIFT MT103 / correspondent bank credit advice evidencing settlement of the export proceeds
Intangible service export dossier for pure digital deliverables: signed outsourcing agreement, IP assignment or licence documentation, delivery logs with timestamps and evidence of client acceptance
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT systematically cross-matches export declarations and zero-rated invoices against the customs SIGE database, VIES intra-EU records and bank foreign-exchange data; any mismatch or documentary gap triggers retroactive recharacterisation of the supply as taxable at 21% plus statutory late-payment interest. Administrative penalties under Arts. 191 and 198 LGT range from 50% to 150% of the under-declared amount, with fixed penalties under Art. 201 LGT of EUR 150 to EUR 300 or 1% per month of VAT where invoice documentation is defective. If the VAT or tax loss exceeds EUR 120,000, criminal tax fraud under Art. 305 Código Penal may result in imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of up to six times the defrauded amount; amounts above EUR 600,000 or committed within an organised group trigger Art. 305bis with sentences of 2 to 6 years. Undue refunds obtained are clawed back within the four-year statute of limitation, and the SL may be suspended from REDEME and lose AEO certification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating as the national competent authority within the European System of Central Banks and the Eurosystem, exercises prudential supervision over Spanish credit institutions, foreign-currency statistical reporting, and balance-of-payments declarations under the capital-movement regime. Administrative and policy authority over cross-border capital flows is shared with the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business, which maintains the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores (Foreign Investment Registry) under Law 19/2003 and Royal Decree-Law 5/2023, as amended by Law 8/2023. Operational AML/CFT oversight of banks and electronic-money institutions is exercised by SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias), the Spanish Financial Intelligence Unit. The Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV) supervises listed issuers, investment services, and FX derivatives providers; for a standard Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada engaged in cross-border 3D art outsourcing, the day-to-day authority is the Bank of Spain through the clearing bank and the foreign-investment registry through the Ministry.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain applies full and unrestricted currency convertibility as a eurozone member state. Both current-account payments (dividends, royalties, service fees, interest, profit remittances) and capital-account operations (equity injections, shareholder loans, loan repayments and repatriation of liquidation proceeds) are liberalised under Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the national implementing framework of Law 19/2003. No exchange-control licence, no prior convertibility approval, and no waiting period is imposed on an SL distributing its after-tax earnings to non-resident shareholders; the only frictions are the ordinary 19% dividend withholding tax applicable to non-resident shareholders and the availability of treaty relief (reduced to between 0% and 10% under EU Directives or the Spain-Latin America double-tax treaties such as Mexico, Argentina, Chile and Colombia). The euro is fully convertible into USD, GBP, JPY or any other globally tradeable currency at market rates through the commercial banks, without central-bank rationing. The remaining compliance burden is informatory rather than authorisation-based: transactions crossing regulatory thresholds must be reported through the Bank of Spain's statistical balance-of-payments form and, where the operation is a foreign direct investment of ten percent or more of the share capital or of control, through the post-transaction statement filed with the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores. For a creative studio invoicing overseas game publishers, no material convertibility or remittance hurdle exists, provided the invoice chain, transfer-pricing file and beneficial-owner register are kept in good order.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no export-proceeds surrender obligations and no mandatory conversion ratios on receipts from exported services. A resident SL supplying 3D sculpting, character rigging and art outsourcing to foreign game publishers may freely keep receivables in USD, GBP, JPY or EUR in domestic foreign-currency accounts, or may leave them offshore with the same tax transparency, subject to correct accounting and declaration in the annual corporate income tax return (Modelo 200). There is no statutory repatriation deadline, no obligation to liquidate foreign balances, and no penalty for retaining export earnings outside the euro area; the Bank of Spain's balance-of-payments declaration applies only to the statistical collection of settlement flows above stated thresholds. The operative compliance duties are: (i) issue of an accurate invoice identifying the non-resident client and the place of supply, (ii) Spanish VAT application under the place-of-supply rule that generally removes B2B digital service income from the Spanish VAT base where the client is a taxable person in another jurisdiction, subject to the Modelo 349 recapitulative statement where required, and (iii) documentation of economic substance sufficient to defeat any allegation of diverted income or passive foreign-investment-company treatment. No surrender certificate, no exchange approval and no conversion receipt is required from the Bank of Spain before the funds are used for treasury or distribution purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (cuenta de capital social) + Corporate Operating Multi-Currency Account (WorldOne or 1|2|3 Business)
Capital Escrow Account + Operating Account with integrated FX portal and automatic hedging module
Capital Escrow Account + Operational and Payroll (nómina) Account with SEPA-native clearing
Operational Current Account with international collection services for EMEA and US receivables
SME Operational Account with remote video-KYC opening; limited structured FX desk
Domestic Operational Account for payroll debits and tax payments; restricted international correspondent network

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: HIGH for collection of receivables and payment of freelance suppliers; MEDIUM-LOW when proposed as the sole treasury interface of the Spanish SL. EU-licensed electronic-money institutions passportable into Spain under PSD2 and Directive 2009/110/EC include Wise (Belgium/Estonia licence), Revolut Business (Lithuania), Airwallex (Netherlands), MultiPass, and Payoneer; US-chartered platforms such as Mercury have no EU passport and may only be used for dollar-denominated flows outside the European treasury structure. EMIs offer swift multi-currency IBANs, low-cost conversion, virtual cards, and instant-payment rails. Legal constraints are material: an EMI is not a credit institution, cannot grant overdrafts, cannot issue commercial letters of credit or bank guarantees, is not covered by the Spanish Fondo de Garantía de Depósitos, and must segregate client funds. Some Spanish counterparties and public authorities require a Spanish domestic IBAN commencing with ES for SEPA direct debits, tax refunds and utility debits, and non-ES IBANs are occasionally refused despite the end of the SEPA IBAN-discrimination regime. The legally prudent blueprint is therefore a two-tier treasury: a tier-1 Spanish bank holding the capital escrow, payroll, tax-payment and borrowing capacity, complemented by one or two EMIs used exclusively for rapid inwards collection from global game publishers and low-value subcontracted art outsourcing payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under Spanish Law 10/2010 on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, banks must apply customer due diligence identifying the legal entity, its statutory directors, and every beneficial owner holding more than twenty-five percent. In practice, Santander, BBVA, CaixaBank and Sabadell uniformly require either (i) physical attendance at a Spanish branch of at least one director or duly empowered secretary for biometric verification at the moment of account opening, or (ii) acceptance of a notarised and apostilled power of attorney together with the certified certificate of incorporation, followed by a live videoconference KYC interview of all beneficial owners. Purely remote account opening without any physical touchpoint is granted only by a minority of desks, typically BBVA and Santander corporate remote onboarding where the SL was incorporated within the previous twelve weeks, the directors have EU tax residency, and projected annual turnover is below one million euros. Given that the target SL has non-resident founders and an external BPO commercial model, the prudent costing assumption is that at least one authorised representative will make a physical visit to Madrid to complete the identity verification; alternatively, the shareholders may appoint a Spanish-resident corporate agent (gestoría or trust desk) holding a notarial power to perform the interview. Digital EMIs are more flexible and allow entirely remote onboarding, but they do not remove the statutory identity obligations and may be weaker for complex treasury operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: non-resident individual beneficial owners resident in multiple LATAM and US jurisdictions, causing the bank to classify the account as enhanced-risk geographical exposure and to request PEPS/PEP-related screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A formally certified KYC bundle comprising: notarised and promote-apostilled passport copies of each beneficial owner; certificado de residencia fiscal from each relevant tax authority; updated professional CVs evidencing game-industry experience; source-of-wealth statement with supporting brokerage and bank statements from the last twelve months; certified charter and shareholders register of the SL; clean sanctions screening against OFAC, EU, UN and UK lists; and an organisational chart evidencing the complete beneficial ownership chain to each natural person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: BPO invoicing pattern showing the SL billing only non-resident affiliated or captive clients at thin margins, suggesting round-tripping, invoice parking, or artificial relocation of profits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master service agreements with non-affiliated game publishers referencing ISIC 7490 activity; detailed statements-of-work and milestones; signed delivery logs from Perforce/Jira or Cool VLAD; aged receivables ledger; OECD-aligned transfer-pricing documentation including a local file in Spanish adopting the Transactional Net Margin Method; legally issued invoices (C11/CI format) with serial numbers; payroll records and Spanish Social Security TC1/TC2 remittances; and the general meeting minutes approving the service commission policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: collection through PayPal and other aggregators as a primary channel, creating mixed fund provenance and making the bank unable to verify the commercial origin of deposits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business PayPal statistical report exported quarterly showing merchant account identity; contractual clauses in the client agreement designating PayPal as an agreed payment rail; reconciliation workbook matching each PayPal settlement to the corresponding issued invoice and contract milestone; a written internal treasury policy capping aggregator receipts at ten thousand euros per invoice; proof of regular sweeping from the aggregator into the tier-1 bank account; and the PSP provider's compliance certificate evidencing merchant KYC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: SL registered at a serviced address without physical office, causing suspicion of artificial substance creation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully scheduled lease agreement or serviced-office licence evidencing occupied workstations; utility bill and municipal register evidence; registration of the definitive CIF/NIF certificates issued by the Tax Agency; certificate of registration in the Registro Mercantil; the Modelo 036 declaration of commencement of activity and IAE industrial trade licence; evidence of payroll and social security filings in Spain; and photographs or contractor details of the production studio where the 3D art is generated.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the incorporation or capital increase of the Spanish SL, the non-resident shareholder routes a SWIFT MT103 from its home bank to the SL's account in Spain, addressing the receiving Spanish bank with remittance information reading 'Equity contribution, Law 19/2003 capital movement' and identifying the ordering customer as the non-resident investing shareholder and the final beneficiary as the SL. Where both legs are in euro, the transfer may alternatively be settled through SEPA Instant Credit Transfer or TIPS, subject to the receiving bank's discretion; SWIFT MT103 is mandatory for cross-border transfers in non-euro currencies. The Spanish bank performs look-through verification of the ultimate origin of funds and files the balance-of-payments declaration with the Banco de España where the inflow exceeds the applicable statistical threshold. Where the investor-company relationship creates a participation of ten percent or more of the share capital, the shareholder must submit the post-transaction declaration to the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores within one month after deposit, a notification rather than an authorisation requirement; no prior screening applies to a non-strategic creative-services company. To defeat desk rejection, the supporting bundle must include the notarial deed of incorporation or capital increase, the notary's certificate of deposit of capital, the updated register certificate from the Registro Mercantil, the shareholders' agreement, and a sworn origin-of-funds statement; the description field must never use 'personal transfer', 'gift', or ambiguous family-support codes because those trigger automatic anti-money-laundering review.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The SL settles outbound trade obligations using three clearing rails. First, SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) in euro for all EU and EEA suppliers, freelancers, and software platforms, settled on the same business day. Second, SWIFT MT103 (with cover in MT202 COV for correspondent-bank legs) for non-EU beneficiaries, especially US-based art directors, Latin American outsourcing vendors, and Asian middleware licensors; ISO 20022 purpose codes recommended are 'SVGS' for general professional service fees, 'SUPP' for materials and supplies, 'LICF' for software licence fees including Unreal Engine and Maya/Blender tool licences, and 'INTC' for intercompany settlements between affiliated entities. Third, irrevocable confirmed documentary letters of credit governed by UCP600 for physical ancillary production such as collectible model manufacturing, packaging art and merchandise, where the bank issues an import LC with acceptance protocols evidenced by signed carrier bills and inspection certificates; pure digital asset deliveries rarely require a commercial LC because the deliverable is a CAD file and the bank needs an acceptance statement instead of bills of lading. For payments to non-resident freelancers without a permanent establishment in Spain, the SL must withhold IRNR under Spanish law at the treaty-adjusted rate (generally twenty-four percent before treaty reduction, or fifteen percent where the freelancer is an EU or EEA resident) and file Modelo 216/240, with the evidence retained in the vendor file year after year.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward exchange contracts against the euro for USD, GBP, JPY, CAD and AUD receivables, executed OTC with the tier-1 bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or long-form corporate master, requiring no exchange-control permission and no margin posting below agreed credit lines

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currencies such as ARS, BRL, MXN, CLP, TRY and INR, cash-settled in euro or USD without physical delivery of the restricted currency, permissible where the underlying service invoice is denominated in the emerging-market currency

Cross-currency swaps matched to the tenor of multi-year development contracts or advance-financing structures, exchanging fixed or floating USD/JPY liability streams into euro and providing synthetic euro funding without disrupting the external cash flow

European-style FX put options on foreign-currency receivables purchased from the bank's markets desk, giving the SL a protected floor conversion rate while retaining upside if the foreign currency appreciates before settlement

Spot FX transactions executed through the bank's electronic portal with automatic straight-through-processing of payment orders, converting client receipts within minutes at interbank-adjacent rates and sweeping the euro proceeds into the domestic operating account

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approve within six months after financial year-end and deposit within one month after approval; for a 31 December year-end, normally by 30 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure and possible administrative penalty of EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, increasing up to EUR 300,000 for entities with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6 million; persistent non-filing may trigger strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the first 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the tax year-end; for a 31 December year-end, normally 1 to 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late self-correction generally incurs a surcharge of 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay, capped at 15%; interest generally applies after 12 months, with additional penalties possible where assessment or enforcement is initiated.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Electronic legalization of accounting and corporate books
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, normally by 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted legalization may impair evidentiary value, generate registry compliance issues, and contribute to inspection or administrative exposure; no automatic annual strike-off is imposed solely for late book legalization.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership declaration accompanying annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry and the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership through applicable registry channels
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted with the annual accounts deposit and updated when beneficial ownership information changes under the applicable statutory reporting period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or missing beneficial ownership information may cause filing rejection, registry compliance measures, and administrative sanctions under Spanish anti-money-laundering legislation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is generally required when the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets of EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover of EUR 5.7 million, or average workforce of more than 50 employees. Additional requirements apply to public-interest entities, listed entities, regulated activities, and certain group or other statutory situations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad) and applicable Spanish commercial accounting rules. IFRS is generally mandatory for consolidated accounts of listed groups and may apply in other legally specified cases; an ordinary Spanish SL normally prepares individual accounts under Spanish GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain has no separate annual UBO return solely confirming shareholding transfers. The company must maintain current beneficial ownership information, submit the beneficial ownership declaration with the annual accounts, and update the information when ownership or control changes. Transfers of SL participations must be recorded in the Register of Members and reflected in the beneficial ownership records where applicable.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Sole Shareholder, if applicable
Register of Directors and Company Secretaries, where applicable

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 325-1,300 per year, depending on registered-office, mail-handling, accounting, and corporate-secretarial services.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,000-8,000 for a small non-regulated SL; materially higher for groups, regulated entities, or complex international operations.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate for newly created eligible companies during the first two tax periods; R&D and technological innovation tax credits; deductions for job creation and intangible asset exploitation under patent box rules; reduced effective rates for small entities on the first tranche of taxable income (subject to annual thresholds)
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (for tax periods commencing on or after 1 January 2016; annual offset limited for very large taxpayers)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) filed electronically via the Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) through the Sede Electrónica (electronic office portal)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months and twenty-five calendar days after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year company, the filing window runs from 1 July to 25 July of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification number (NIF) of the Spanish limited liability company, corporate name, registered office, and financial year-end
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not file this form; the Spanish SL must report its own NIF and corporate data. Shareholder residency is disclosed separately via beneficial ownership declarations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit or loss before tax adjustments, derived from the statutory profit and loss account prepared under Spanish GAAP
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign parent or service recipient must not commingle its own accounts here; all amounts must relate solely to the Spanish operational entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Boxes 00310-00360 (correction of accounting result and permanent/temporary adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Extract from the reconciliation between accounting result and taxable income, including depreciation, amortisation, provisions, and non-deductible expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border service fees paid to the Spanish entity must be arm's length; penalty or default interest charges and fictitious expenses must be adjusted as permanent differences.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income for the Spanish corporate income tax after application of carryforwards, set-offs, and regime adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This figure is the foundation for the final tax liability. A non-resident shareholder cannot use losses or credits of the Spanish company in its own jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computed by applying the applicable rate (generally 25%) to the taxable base, before deductions and credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any withholding tax credit or treaty relief relevant to foreign shareholders is not handled in this box; it is applied separately when the dividend is distributed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepayments of corporate income tax, instalment payments made during the year, and any withholdings suffered by the company
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot reclaim these amounts; instalment payments are the exclusive obligation of the Spanish entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final net amount payable or refundable, including any self-assessment adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be settled in euro from a Spanish bank account or by direct debit. Failure to pay triggers enforced collection and surcharges.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior AEAT notice: progressive i) 5% unpaid if filed within 3 months late; ii) 10% within 3-6 months; iii) 15% within 6-12 months; iv) 20% after 12 months, plus default interest. If filed after AEAT notice, the penalty ranges from 50% to 150% of the lost tax. Non-filing without tax loss attracts fixed penalties from EUR 300 to EUR 10,000 depending on turnover; filing after official request triggers additional sanctions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% final withholding tax on dividends and profit distributions paid to non-resident shareholders, unless a domestic exemption, EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, or double tax treaty reduces the rate (commonly 0-10%).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must submit a valid certificate of tax residence (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) from its own competent tax authority to the Spanish paying entity before or at the time of distribution. The Spanish payer must retain a copy in its transfer pricing and withholding tax file. If the rate is not reduced at source, the shareholder may claim a refund through Modelo 210/211 against proof of residence and beneficial ownership. Beneficial ownership form and prior-session agreements may be required. Treaty relief is denied where the shareholder is a conduit without substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory withholding 19% for non-residents; 0% under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive when paid to a qualifying associated company (direct 25% holding) resident in another EU jurisdiction. Royalties (IP use): statutory withholding 19% for non-residents; treaty rates typically 5-10% and 0% under the same EU Directive for qualifying related parties. Domestic exemptions apply to certain public debt and bank interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required for taxpayers with annual turnover exceeding EUR 10,000,000 that carry out related-party transactions; Master File required for entities belonging to a multi-national group with consolidated turnover above EUR 20,000,000 (or lower EU-derived thresholds). Any cross-border related-party transaction individually exceeding EUR 100,000 must be disclosed annually in Modelo 232 and be supported by contemporaneous functional and risk analysis.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations. However, the Spanish General Anti-Abuse Rule (Ley 58/2003, article 15), the European ATAD anti-abuse rules, and the CFC regime require real economic substance: physical office or establishment in Spain, actual employees and decision-making, and a genuine business purpose. Lack of substance is a decisive factor in re-characterising the Spanish SL as a resident shell, denying treaty benefits, and imposing penalties under the anti-avoidance framework.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (Infracción tributaria grave / Delito contra la Hacienda Pública)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting income, inflating deductible expenses, using fictitious invoices, or structuring payments to non-resident entities without economic justification in the corporate income tax returns for more than EUR 120,000 of defrauded tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 50% to 150% of the under-declared tax plus default interest; if criminal evasion is established, imprisonment of 2 to 6 years, a fine of up to six times the defrauded amount, and loss of public subsidies or benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, de facto managers, or legal representatives may be personally liable for the unpaid tax under LGT article 42. In criminal cases, the same persons are criminally responsible for the evasion; the corporate veil is pierced for assets acquired with the defrauded amount, and travel bans or provisional imprisonment can be ordered.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abuse of Legal Form (Abuso de forma y simulación)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a Spanish SL with no office, no employees, no local decision-making, and no genuine commercial activity, used solely as an invoicing vehicle to shift profits derived from game art assets to non-resident related parties or low-tax jurisdictions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT re-characterises the transaction under the GAAR: taxable income is recalculated, treaty relief is denied, and a penalty surcharge of 20% to 40% applies to the corrected tax. Intragroup payments to blacklisted or non-cooperative jurisdictions may face a special 19% withholding tax at gross, with no credit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participated in or installed the shell structure are jointly liable for the resulting tax debt. Criminal tax or money laundering proceedings can be joined; the court may disable the director from managing other companies and seize personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register the beneficial ownership of the Spanish SL with the Spanish Companies Register (BOE / Registro de Titularidades Reales), accepting wire transfers or PayPal revenues without underlying service contracts, or tolerating unexplained third-party payments without AML customer due diligence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under AML Law 10/2010: minor infringements EUR 300 to EUR 150,000; serious infringements EUR 150,000 to EUR 600,000; very serious infringements up to EUR 5,000,000 or 5% of the offender's turnover. Criminal money laundering independently carries imprisonment up to 6 years and confiscation of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for AML penalties where they knowingly carried out or ordered the operation. Criminal conviction for money laundering leads to personal imprisonment, disqualification from professional practice, and separate monetary fines. In serious cases, the corporate veil is disregarded and directors may face travel bans and preventive seizure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Prepare Transfer Pricing Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Not maintaining a contemporaneous Local File, Master File, or Modelo 232 disclosure when the Spanish entity engages in cross-border related-party transactions exceeding the applicable thresholds (e.g., service payments or art outsourcing fees above EUR 100,000)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of EUR 1,500 to EUR 50,000 per missing or incomplete documentation set; in addition, AEAT may perform a unilateral adjustment and apply a 15% to 20% surcharge on the corrected tax. The company cannot rely on the arm's length standard without compliant documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who certifies or approves the tax return is directly responsible for the inaccuracy; if the TP adjustments lead to under-declared tax, the personal joint liability regime under LGT article 42.1(a) applies, with civil liability and procedural interception orders.
